title: Blood Bank Equipment (Refrigerator, Platelet Agitator & Component Storage)

references.label: AABB Technical Manual
references.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Blood & Biotherapies (AABB)

purpose: A small family of dedicated storage/handling equipment — blood bank refrigerators, platelet agitators, and related component-storage devices — maintains blood components within the narrow temperature and handling conditions each component type requires to remain safe and viable for transfusion.
operatingPrinciple: Different blood components have different storage requirements because they degrade differently: red cells are stored refrigerated (a narrow cold range) to slow metabolic degradation while remaining viable; platelets, in contrast, are stored at room temperature under continuous gentle agitation, since refrigeration and stillness both damage platelet function; plasma/cryoprecipitate is stored frozen to preserve labile clotting factors. Dedicated blood bank refrigerators and freezers (distinct from general-purpose lab units) include continuous temperature monitoring and alarm systems specifically because a temperature excursion can render a component unsafe or unusable without any visible change to the unit.
basicOperation: Continuously monitor and log temperature (or agitation, for platelets) per the component-specific requirement, with alarms for any excursion outside the validated range.
Segregate units appropriately (e.g. by component type, crossmatch/reservation status) per the laboratory's chain-of-custody procedure.
Inspect units for integrity, correct labeling, and expiration before release for transfusion.
importantSettings: Target temperature range specific to the component type stored
calibration: Temperature probes and alarm systems are verified and calibrated on a defined schedule per the laboratory's equipment management program, with continuous monitoring providing ongoing verification between formal calibrations.
maintenance: Regular cleaning and defrost/maintenance cycles per manufacturer schedule, performed without allowing stored components to exceed their required temperature range during the process.
Battery backup/alarm system function testing on a defined schedule.

commonErrors.cause: Door left ajar, power interruption, or unit malfunction
commonErrors.fix: Follow the laboratory's excursion procedure — assess affected units per component-specific stability rules before any release for transfusion

commonErrors.problem: Platelet unit swirling pattern lost on visual inspection
commonErrors.cause: Inadequate agitation or extended storage beyond validated shelf life
commonErrors.fix: Do not release the unit; follow the laboratory's component-quality rejection procedure

safety: All blood components are biohazardous — handle spills and unit disposal per biohazard protocol.
Follow the facility's chain-of-custody and component-release documentation procedures without exception.
